note: 390px viewport, 105 pages. Findings marked seenIn:ci reproduce on the CI runner and NOT on macOS — the three institution-public pages overflow by exactly 10px there (scrollWidth 400 against a 390 viewport) and the team page reads 621 rather than 610. The difference is real and measured; a local run reports them as no longer reproducing, which is how the divergence stays visible. Overflow findings carry a magnitude (the measured scrollWidth, higher is worse) and fail the run if they grow. Where the two machines disagree the WORSE reading is recorded — the team page at 621, not the 610 this laptop measures — because a magnitude taken on one machine would otherwise fail the other on the machine difference rather than on a regression. The cost of that choice is that a local degradation from 610 up to 621 passes.
